headline: Light showers linger Sunday and dense fog may form early Monday, then a warm Monday (low 60s to low 70s) gives way to cooler weather from Tuesday on, with widespread, mostly beneficial rain likely Wednesday into Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Around Charlotte and across the region, a cool, damp layer of air trapped against the mountains keeps skies cloudy with scattered light showers overnight and through much of Sunday, and lingering gusty winds in the South Carolina Upstate ease by mid to late morning. Showers wind down by Sunday evening as that cool air erodes, the rain-producing lift shuts off and dry conditions return. With clouds thinning, light winds and leftover low-level moisture, widespread patchy to dense fog is increasingly likely Sunday night into daybreak Monday, possibly with very low visibility.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Once Monday's fog lifts, the day turns noticeably warm ahead of a cold front, with highs in the low 60s to low 70s and a few spots in the southern Upstate nearing the mid 70s. The front crosses Monday night into Tuesday morning mostly dry, apart from a few mountain showers mainly along the Tennessee border. A large high-pressure system then spreads in, bringing dry, cooler northeast winds and more typical late-November temperatures Tuesday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cool, seasonable air stays in place through the rest of the week as another wedge of cool air sets up east of the mountains. Rain chances keep trending up for midweek: a storm system from the south is expected to form along the Carolina coast and strengthen as it moves up the coast, pushing plenty of moist ocean air inland, and confidence is increasing in widespread rain Wednesday into Thursday. For now it looks like a beneficial rain with no hazards expected, though that could change as computer models settle on how the storm develops.

watch_for: Dense fog Sunday night into Monday morning could make for a slow, low-visibility commute.
Wednesday–Thursday storm: widespread rain is increasingly likely; currently no hazards expected, but details could change as models come into agreement.
confidence: Forecasters sound fairly settled on Sunday's showers ending and a warm Monday, and the odds of dense fog Monday morning have gone up; confidence is increasing in widespread rain Wednesday into Thursday, but how the midweek storm evolves, and whether it brings any hazards, is still uncertain.
